I get this overwhelming urge to eat, like I can't stop thinking about food, and then I end up consuming huge amounts—entire boxes of cookies, whole pizzas, ice cream by the pint—all in a few hours, late at night after my last student leaves. I keep snacks hidden in my studio because I don’t want anyone to know. I eat until I’m in pain, so full I can barely move, but I still can’t stop.

I feel so ashamed afterward, like I’m losing control. The worst part is, I’ve been having these intense bursts of energy lately—times when I can’t sleep for hours, talk really fast, clean the whole apartment at 3 a.m., or start ambitious music projects I never finish. But they don’t last long—just a few days, not a full week. I’ve never had a full manic episode that disrupted my work or required hospitalization, and I don’t have deep depressive crashes after. The last few months especially, I’ve had these bursts of energy. Stayed up three nights in a row reorganizing the boat, painting the deck—didn’t feel tired. Talked fast, maybe too much. I can’t say if it’s stress, age, or something else. Some weeks I’m fine. Others, it’s like I’m not in the wheelhouse of my own life. My wife’s worried, and honestly… so am I. But I can’t tell if this is just bad patches or something more.

To be honest, I’ve also felt unusually energized lately—like I don’t need as much sleep, ideas racing, talking fast, cleaning the whole house late at night. My wife mentioned it, said I seemed “wired.” But it doesn’t last—maybe a couple days, then it fades. I never get reckless with money, haven’t had any psychotic moments, and I’m not cycling into deep lows. The eating episodes are what worry me most—they’re out of control, and I feel ashamed after. The high energy stuff? It’s there, but not severe enough to be a full manic episode, I think.
